question: Can a cavity-sensitive face readout distinguish hollow AW5 from filled AW5 under declared dynamics?
assumptions: Oriented real simplicial chain model with unit simplex inner product
target_exposure: Offline flux, shielding, routing and matter/vacuum ideas exposed before intake replay
sources: User-supplied offline LLM report; citation keys unresolved
baseline: Filled AW5 under matching model and readout
result: Unit-cell bench intake v1 scores loopback, signed basis injections and held-out comparisons. Five synthetic cases and CLI receipt verified. Bench evidence OPEN.
next_discriminant: Collect signed pair bench data and audit timestamp, endpoint and scope certificates.

supporting_results.result: Exact plus-sign cavity formula; legal filled 2-to-3 control changes the finite-time face spectrum and preserves b2=0.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Apply a boundary-fixed refinement to hollow AW5 and separate lifetime, external readout residue and harmonic count.

supporting_results.result: Boundary-fixed refinement preserves b2=1 but moves the original exterior residue from 1/4 to 19/80; best aligned residue is 91/380 after one leaf.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Derive a metric-aware refinement and readout-transfer rule, or exhibit an obstruction.

supporting_results.result: Exact split metric with matched drive/readout preserves 1/4 at any finite depth. The normalized raw exterior and Euclidean Whitney controls differ. Refined-carrier scoring remains open.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Derive and freeze a finite-window contrast bound for an identified refined carrier and its actual exterior readout.

supporting_results.result: One-leaf AW5 model contrast against each control is at least 978548309/16095641600 with joint confidence at least 1-2 exp(-16) under stated acquisition tolerances.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Replay the refined model traces through the frozen scorer and bind the identified probe map to calibration evidence.

supporting_results.result: Frozen one-leaf synthetic packet passes both contrasts at gamma=1/512; committed envelope and packet hashes verified before reveal.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Bind the refined probe map to calibrated hardware records, starting with signed-pair timing and basis shots.

supporting_results.result: First-level subsets guarantee contrast >= 7/100. Uniform depth 3 clears 3/64 with direct damped enclosure. Static residue equals 1/[2(1+(3/2)^d)] and tends to zero.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Derive frequency-dependent four-terminal reduction or an equivalent certified method for depth four and beyond.

supporting_results.result: Four-face terminal response exists after shared graded assembly; the recursive 14-coordinate leaf ports and final 16-face AW5 resolvent certify the original gate at uniform depths 4–6. Depth-six margin is 0.000240.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Tighten the depth-six numerical enclosure and test whether depth seven clears the fixed gate.

supporting_results.result: Depth-six lower bound 0.060216. Depth-seven undamped fixed-reference gap encloses [0.082828,0.086642], but an admissible Gaussian witness violates the uniform failure level under the original budget.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Derive a sharper noise or deterministic budget for the fixed-reference contrast and identify its spectral weight.

supporting_results.result: The depth-seven target is exactly edge-free. Two interval-verified constant-terminal modes contribute +0.083500 and +0.033991; the differential sector offsets part of the positive top-cell transient.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Lift the selected eigenvectors and measure their norm distribution by refinement level and cell orbit.

supporting_results.result: Mode A is nodeless and nearly uniform. Mode B is sign-changing and shell-dominated. The internal shared-face dual-cycle projection vanishes exactly for both lifts.
supporting_results.next_discriminant: Lift the first-order response to a one-leaf perturbation and test the shell and dual-cycle observables under the same probe.
